question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

ZL, WF, TZ, QT, NN, KH, ?, EV
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. HB.

GIVEN

• ZL, WF, TZ, QT, NN, KH, ?, EV

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: Z(26), W(23), T(20), Q(17), N(14), K(11), ?, E(5) — each −3 ⇒ ? = 11−3 = 8 = H.

• 2nd letters: L(12), F(6), Z(26), T(20), N(14), H(8), ?, V(22) — each −6 ⇒ ? = 8−6 = 2 = B.

• Missing term = HB.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Split into two independent columns: first letters step −3, second letters step −6; just continue each.

NOTE

• Use position numbers A=1…Z=26; when the value goes below 1, add 26 (0→Z, −1→Y).

question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and sixth letter cluster is related to fifth letter cluster.

DJ : ZC :: YF : ? :: KI : GB
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. UY.

GIVEN

• DJ : ZC :: YF : ? :: KI : GB

SOLUTION

• Check DJ → ZC: D(4)−4 = 0 = 26 = Z; J(10)−7 = C(3). So rule: 1st letter −4, 2nd letter −7.

• Verify KI → GB: K(11)−4 = G(7); I(9)−7 = B(2). ✓

• Apply to YF: Y(25)−4 = 21 = U; F(6)−7 = −1 = 25 = Y ⇒ UY.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Find the shift from an easy pair (KI→GB gives −4, −7) and apply the same shift to YF.

NOTE

• On negative results wrap around by adding 26; keep each letter's shift independent.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(RE, OB, LY)

(EY, BV, YE)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (EU, BR, YI).

GIVEN

• Sample set (RE, OB, LY): first letters R(18), O(15), L(12) → each −3; the two letters of every cluster are also a fixed gap apart.

SOLUTION

• Required rule: the first letters of the three clusters must step −3, and the internal gap between the two letters must stay constant.

• Option (EU, BR, YI): first letters E(5), B(2), Y(25) → −3 each (2−3 = −1 = 25 = Y). Internal gap = 16 in all three (U−E, R−B, |I−Y|). ✓

• Options 1, 2, 4 break the −3 step on the first letters.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Read only the first letter of each cluster in the option; the one whose first letters go −3, −3 is the answer.

NOTE

• In 'same-rule' sets both the between-cluster shift and the within-cluster gap must be uniform.

question: What will be the product of the number of Tuesdays and Wednesdays in the month of October in the year 2015?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 16.

GIVEN

• Month = October 2015 (31 days).

SOLUTION

• 1 October 2015 was a Thursday.

• 31 = 4 weeks + 3 extra days, so the first three weekdays (Thu, Fri, Sat) occur 5 times; all others occur 4 times.

• Tuesday and Wednesday are not among the extra days ⇒ each occurs 4 times.

• Product = 4 × 4 = 16.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• In a 31-day month only the first 3 weekdays get 5; every other day = 4. Here 4 × 4 = 16.

NOTE

• A day repeats 5 times only if it falls on day 1, 2 or 3 of a 31-day month (1 or 2 for 30-day).

question: If 10 June 2012 was Sunday, then what day was it on 10 October 2012?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Wednesday.

GIVEN

• 10 June 2012 = Sunday. Find the day on 10 October 2012.

SOLUTION

• Days from 10 Jun to 10 Oct = 30 (Jun) + 31 (Jul) + 31 (Aug) + 30 (Sep) = 122 days.

• 122 ÷ 7 = 17 remainder 3 (odd days).

• Sunday + 3 = Wednesday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Count only the remainder of total days ÷ 7 (here 3) and move that many weekdays forward.

NOTE

• Month day-counts to the same date next month: Jun 30, Jul 31, Aug 31, Sep 30; 2012 being a leap year doesn't affect Jun–Oct.

question: 5 persons P, Q, R, S and T are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). P and R are sitting at the extreme ends of the row. S is sitting to the immediate right of R. Q is sitting second to the left of P. What is the position of T in the given seating arrangement?
option_1: Second from the left end of the row
option_2: Third from the left end of the row
option_3: Second from the right end of the row
option_4: Third from the right end of the row
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Second from the right end of the row.

GIVEN

• 5 persons in a row facing north; P & R at the extreme ends; S immediately right of R; Q second to left of P.

SOLUTION

• Facing north, right = east side. S is immediately right of R, so R must be at the left end (position 1) and P at the right end (position 5).

• S right of R ⇒ position 2 = S.

• Q is second to the left of P(5) ⇒ position 3 = Q.

• Remaining position 4 = T.

• Order (left→right): R, S, Q, T, P. T is 2nd from the right end.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 'Immediate right of R' needs a seat to R's right, so R can't be the right end — fix R at left, P at right, then fill S and Q.

NOTE

• For a north-facing row, the person's right is the east (higher-numbered) side; reverse it for a south-facing row.

question: Height of 6 girls P, Q, R, S, T and U is compared. Height of no two girls is same. R is taller than only four girls. U is taller than both S and P. S and P both are taller than both Q and T. Who is the tallest girl among these 6 girls?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. U.

GIVEN

• R taller than only 4 girls; U > S and U > P; S, P > Q and T.

SOLUTION

• 'R taller than only four' ⇒ exactly one girl is taller than R, so R is 2nd tallest.

• U > S, P and S, P > Q, T, so U sits above S, P, Q, T.

• The single girl above R must be U ⇒ order: U > R > S, P > Q, T.

• Tallest = U.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 'Taller than exactly 4 out of 6' = rank 2, so the tallest is whoever beats R — that is U.

NOTE

• Convert phrases like 'taller than only n girls' directly into a rank: rank = (total − n).

question:
Select the option that is related to the first letter-number cluster in the same way as the fourth letter-number cluster is related to the third letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

EJ18 : ? :: LT20 : RJ400 :: SK22 : IQ484
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. HC324.

GIVEN

• EJ18 : ? :: LT20 : RJ400 :: SK22 : IQ484

SOLUTION

• LT20 → RJ400: reverse letters L,T → T,L then subtract 2 each: T(20)−2 = R(18), L(12)−2 = J(10) = RJ; number 20² = 400.

• SK22 → IQ484: reverse S,K → K,S, −2 each: K(11)−2 = I(9), S(19)−2 = Q(17) = IQ; number 22² = 484. ✓

• Rule: swap the two letters, subtract 2 from each, and square the number.

• EJ18: reverse E,J → J,E, −2 each: J(10)−2 = H(8), E(5)−2 = C(3) = HC; number 18² = 324 ⇒ HC324.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Number is always the square (18²=324) — that alone points to HC324.

NOTE

• Watch for 'reverse then shift' combos in letter-number analogies; test the number rule (square here) first to eliminate options.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

KJT12 : MMO143 :: ? : LTP168 :: CFP16 : EIK255
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. JQU13.

GIVEN

• KJT12 : MMO143 :: ? : LTP168 :: CFP16 : EIK255

SOLUTION

• Rule (from KJT12→MMO143 & CFP16→EIK255): 1st letter +2, 2nd letter +3, 3rd letter −5; number → n²−1.

• Check: K+2 = M, J+3 = M, T−5 = O; 12²−1 = 143. ✓  C+2 = E, F+3 = I, P−5 = K; 16²−1 = 255. ✓

• Need ? such that ? → LTP168. Reverse the rule on LTP168: number 168 = 13²−1 ⇒ n = 13.

• Letters: 1st +2 = L ⇒ L−2 = J; 2nd +3 = T ⇒ T−3 = Q; 3rd −5 = P ⇒ P+5 = U ⇒ JQU13.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Number 168 = 13²−1 fixes the number as 13, matching only JQU13.

NOTE

• When the unknown is the input, invert each operation (+2 becomes −2, square−1 becomes √(n+1)).

question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and sixth number is related to fifth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

8823 : 8867 :: 6279 : ? :: 7576 : 7620
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 6323.

GIVEN

• 8823 : 8867 :: 6279 : ? :: 7576 : 7620

SOLUTION

• 8823 → 8867: difference = +44.

• 7576 → 7620: difference = 7620 − 7576 = +44. ✓

• Apply to 6279: 6279 + 44 = 6323.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Same constant is added throughout: 8867−8823 = 44, so 6279+44 = 6323.

NOTE

• For number analogies, first test a simple constant difference or ratio before trying complex rules.

question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and third number is related to fourth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

222 : 673 :: 923 : 2776 :: ? : 268
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 87.

GIVEN

• 222 : 673 :: 923 : 2776 :: ? : 268

SOLUTION

• 222 → 673: 222 × 3 + 7 = 666 + 7 = 673.

• 923 → 2776: 923 × 3 + 7 = 2769 + 7 = 2776. ✓  Rule: × 3 + 7.

• ? × 3 + 7 = 268 ⇒ ? × 3 = 261 ⇒ ? = 87.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the rule on 268: (268 − 7) ÷ 3 = 87.

NOTE

• Find the forward rule from the known pairs, then invert it to get an unknown input.

question: In a certain coded language 'ROTA' is coded as 'SPUB' and 'POOR' is coded as 'QPPS'. How will 'TAPA' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. UBQB.

GIVEN

• ROTA → SPUB; POOR → QPPS.

SOLUTION

• ROTA → SPUB: R+1 = S, O+1 = P, T+1 = U, A+1 = B. Every letter shifts +1.

• POOR → QPPS: P+1 = Q, O+1 = P, O+1 = P, R+1 = S. ✓

• TAPA: T+1 = U, A+1 = B, P+1 = Q, A+1 = B ⇒ UBQB.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Simple +1 cipher — just move every letter one step forward.

NOTE

• Confirm the shift on the given repeated letters (both A→B, O→P) before coding the target word.

question: In a certain code language, 'people like ujjain' is coded as 'pn ts dp', 'ujjain has temples' is coded as 'dp tm pq', and 'temples used for' is coded as 'pq rm dt,'. How will 'ujjain temples' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. dp pq.

GIVEN

• people like ujjain → pn ts dp

• ujjain has temples → dp tm pq

• temples used for → pq rm dt

SOLUTION

• 'ujjain' is common to lines 1 and 2; common code = dp ⇒ ujjain = dp.

• 'temples' is common to lines 2 and 3; common code = pq ⇒ temples = pq.

• So 'ujjain temples' = dp pq.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Match the shared word across two lines to its shared code — dp = ujjain, pq = temples.

NOTE

• In message coding, intersect the words and codes of any two sentences that share a word to lock that code.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

AC101, CE285, ?, GI653, IK837
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. EG469.

GIVEN

• AC101, CE285, ?, GI653, IK837

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: A(1), C(3), ?, G(7), I(9) — step +2 ⇒ ? = 5 = E.

• 2nd letters: C(3), E(5), ?, I(9), K(11) — step +2 ⇒ ? = 7 = G.

• Numbers: 101, 285, ?, 653, 837 — difference +184 ⇒ ? = 285 + 184 = 469 (653 = 469 + 184 ✓).

• Missing term = EG469.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Both letters go +2 and numbers go +184; fill the gap straight from the pattern.

NOTE

• Treat letters and numbers as separate arithmetic progressions in mixed alphanumeric series.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

BOA8, FSE12, JWI18, ?, REQ40.5
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. NAM27.

GIVEN

• BOA8, FSE12, JWI18, ?, REQ40.5

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: B(2), F(6), J(10), ?, R(18) — step +4 ⇒ ? = 14 = N.

• 2nd letters: O(15), S(19), W(23), ?, E(5) — step +4 (mod 26) ⇒ ? = 27 → 1 = A (then 31→5 = E ✓).

• 3rd letters: A(1), E(5), I(9), ?, Q(17) — step +4 ⇒ ? = 13 = M.

• Numbers: 8, 12, 18, ?, 40.5 — ratio × 1.5 ⇒ ? = 18 × 1.5 = 27 (27 × 1.5 = 40.5 ✓).

• Missing term = NAM27.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Letters step +4 in each column; numbers multiply by 1.5 — gives NAM27 at once.

NOTE

• A fractional last term (40.5) signals a multiplicative (×1.5) number pattern, not additive.

question: In 12 hours, how many times minute and hour hands of a clock overlap?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 11.

GIVEN

• Overlaps of minute and hour hands in 12 hours.

SOLUTION

• The minute hand laps the hour hand; in 12 hours they coincide once every 12/11 hours.

• Number of overlaps = 11 (the overlap near 12 is shared, so it is not 12).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• In 12 hours hands overlap 11 times; in 24 hours, 22 times.

NOTE

• Hands are also opposite (180°) 11 times and at right angles 22 times in 12 hours.

question: Angle between minute hand and hour hand of a clock at 6:10 and 7:20 are J and K respectively. What is the absolute difference (in degrees) between J and K?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 25.

GIVEN

• Angles at 6:10 (= J) and 7:20 (= K); find |J − K|.

SOLUTION

• Angle formula: |30H − 5.5M|.

• At 6:10 ⇒ |30×6 − 5.5×10| = |180 − 55| = 125° = J.

• At 7:20 ⇒ |30×7 − 5.5×20| = |210 − 110| = 100° = K.

• |J − K| = |125 − 100| = 25°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Use θ = |30H − 5.5M| for each time, then subtract.

NOTE

• If the formula gives more than 180°, subtract from 360° to get the actual angle.

question: The present ages of A, B and C are 20 years, 26 years and 32 years respectively. What was the ratio of ages of A, B and C, 8 years ago from present?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2 : 3 : 4.

GIVEN

• Present ages A = 20, B = 26, C = 32.

SOLUTION

• 8 years ago: A = 20 − 8 = 12, B = 26 − 8 = 18, C = 32 − 8 = 24.

• Ratio 12 : 18 : 24, divide by 6 = 2 : 3 : 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Subtract 8 from each age and cancel the common factor (6).

NOTE

• 'x years ago' subtracts x from every present age before forming the ratio.

question: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 100 years. 10 years ago from present, their ages were in the ratio of 3 : 1. What will be the respective ratio of the ages of father and son after 12 years from present?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 41 : 21.

GIVEN

• Father + Son (present) = 100; 10 years ago ratio = 3 : 1.

SOLUTION

• 10 years ago total = 100 − 20 = 80; split 3 : 1 ⇒ Father = 60, Son = 20.

• Present: Father = 70, Son = 30.

• After 12 years: Father = 82, Son = 42 ⇒ 82 : 42 = 41 : 21.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Bring the sum back 10 years (100−20 = 80), divide 3:1 (60,20), then add years and reduce.

NOTE

• When moving both ages back n years, reduce the combined sum by 2n before applying the ratio.

question: The ratio of the present ages of L and S is 7 : 4. After 10 years from present L's age will be 31 years. What will be the ratio of respective ages of L and S after 15 years from present?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 4 : 3.

GIVEN

• Present L : S = 7 : 4; L + 10 = 31.

SOLUTION

• L (present) = 31 − 10 = 21.

• L : S = 7 : 4, and L = 21 = 7×3 ⇒ S = 4×3 = 12.

• After 15 years: L = 36, S = 27 ⇒ 36 : 27 = 4 : 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• From L = 21 the multiple is 3, so S = 12; add 15 to each and reduce 36:27 = 4:3.

NOTE

• Use one known age to fix the ratio's common multiple, then find the other age instantly.
